title: AI Techlead
description:
At a glance
Our AI team builds GenAI applications that go into production at one of the Netherlands' largest banks. Voice agents handling thousands of contact center calls. AI lending assistants supporting lenders in writing credit proposals. Agentic workflows that actually make it to users.
We don't stop at prototypes. We build, ship, measure, iterate, and do it fast. As an
AI Tech Lead
, you set the technical direction across these initiatives and stay close enough to the code to keep that pace honest. If you've got 7+ years of engineering experience, a serious track record of shipping AI in production, and you're looking to lead at a scale most companies won't give you for years, read on.
Your job
You set the technical direction on GenAI initiatives that span the bank: from the first conversation with a business team through to production and beyond. You decide how things get built, you build with the team, and you make sure the right things actually get done in a complex organisation. Your focus shifts with the use case: backend, frontend, from leveraging LLM’s to agentic. You own outcomes, not just architecture diagrams. You work directly with the people whose problems you're solving, and you bring the rest of the team along.
Concretely, you'll:
Set the technical direction for GenAI solutions across banking use cases: Voice AI, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, document intelligence.
Drive initiatives end-to-end through a complex organisation: align stakeholders, unblock teams, make the calls that need to be made.
Co-create use cases with business counterparts: you understand the problem, not just the technology, and you shape what gets built.
Stay hands-on: design and write the hard parts if required.
Own architecture and technical quality across multiple workstreams: trade-offs, patterns, what we standardise on, what we don't.
Work with Agents, plain LLMs, code, Databricks and whatever the right tool is for the job.
Raise the technical bar of the team: code reviews, design reviews, knowledge sharing, coaching mediors and juniors.
Working environment
You'll be part of a 25+ person AI team inside ABN AMRO's Innovation department. We operate with a startup mindset within a bank that serves millions of customers and employs thousands of individuals: fast feedback loops, direct lines to business leadership, and real deployment at scale. Amsterdam, hybrid.
Your profile
We don't hire on CV titles. We hire on what you've shipped and what you've led. The team includes people who came through software engineering, data science, infra — what they share is proven AI expertise and a bias for building over theorising. As a tech lead, you bring the same plus the ability to take an ambiguous problem and a group of strong engineers and turn it into something running in production.
What you've done:
Led the technical side of AI or software initiatives end-to-end: you've owned the architecture, made the hard calls, and shipped.
Built and deployed AI applications using LLMs, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, voice AI, or equivalent (at production scale, with real users).
Written Python that runs in production: you're a developer, not a notebook user, and you still enjoy writing the code.
Worked with cloud infrastructure: Azure preferred, AWS or GCP also fine.
Operated inside a complex organisation (or built the muscle elsewhere) and got things done across teams, not just within one.
How you work:
You take ambiguous problems, set a direction, and bring people with you (without waiting for permission).
You have strong technical opinions, formed through experience, and you're willing to defend them and change them.
You're as interested in the business problem as in the technical solution.
You explain your decisions clearly to people who don't share your context (engineers, business, leadership).
You follow the GenAI field closely because you're genuinely curious, not because you have to.
You've built something on the side (a tool, a project, a contribution) that shows you don't wait to be told what to learn.
We are offering
We believe it is important to be a good employer. Joining us means stepping into a role with impact, supported by excellent employment conditions that foster your job satisfaction, development, and wellbeing. In addition, we offer:
An attractive gross monthly salary based on a 36‑hour work week, including holiday allowance and a flexible benefit budget which adds up to a range of €65.000 to €93.000 a year based on a 36-hour week (40 hours possible, pro-rated)
An excellent pension scheme, ensuring that you are well prepared for the future.
Flexibility in working: working from home is possible in consultation with your team and depending on your role. We will provide an ergonomic home office setup for you.
Plenty of room for relaxation with five weeks of vacation per year, supplemented by two mandatory days off. You can also purchase up to four additional weeks of vacation annually.
Five “Banking for better days”: extra days off that you can use for personal development or volunteer work.
Personal development is key: you receive a development budget of €1,000 per year, which can accumulate up to €3,000.
An annual public transport pass with free public transportation throughout the Netherlands for both business and private use.
You can find more information about our employment conditions and salary scales in our Collective Labour Agreement (CLA), which applies to this vacancy.
Interested?
No motivation letter. Please answer these two questions instead:
Tell us about an AI initiative you led: what did you build, what calls did you make as the technical lead, and what did you learn when it hit production (or real users)?
What's the most interesting thing you've built or experimented with in AI in the last six months? Why does it matter to you?
Applications without these answers will not be reviewed.
The recruitmentprocess consists of an online personality assessment, an online culture interview, a technical case and an offline technical Interview.

Banking for better, for generations to come.
" Equal opportunities for everyone are a crucial foundation, as we strive for an inclusive culture where all employees feel seen, heard, and valued. Our vision of
being a personal bank in the digital age
aligns perfectly with the demand for surprising insights and innovative solutions, born from a diverse interplay of cultures and experiences. Are you a pioneering data scientist who likes to think outside-the-box?
Would you like to drive new data science solutions to tackle financial fraud?

Your job
As a data scientist, in the Grid Channel Security, you will work together with fraud experts, data scientists, machine learning engineers and data analysts to safeguard our customers from criminals. This includes threats such as phishing, account takeover, lost or stolen debit cards, e-commerce fraud, and more.
Your role will encompass analysing diverse data sources to get actionable insights. This analysis will include, but not limited to, understanding fraud trends across various payment channels, evaluating the potential of different data fields to enhance our fraud detection, experimenting with different modelling approaches and enhancements, recognizing seasonal patterns, and creating reliable forecasts. Your contributions will extend beyond immediate solutions, serving as a catalyst for ongoing improvements in our fraud detection capabilities through model experimentation and the integration of new data elements. In addition to your focused problem-solving efforts, you will be collaborating with others to brainstorm how data science solutions can help us stay one step ahead of criminals in the ongoing cat-and-mouse game.
ABN AMRO is a future driven bank that is working continuously on unlocking the power of data: you will be part of this transformation!

Grid Channel Security within Corporate Information Security Office (CISO) is responsible for the prevention and detection of payment fraud, and deciding the policy and strategy in the area of fraud. The Fraud Monitoring team that you are going to be part of, is a motivated multidisciplinary group of approximately 25 colleagues working with a focus on protecting customers. We work in a hybrid way and our day to day work is organized by the agile and scrum principles. title: Data Analyst - Transaction Banking

Samenwerken met multidisciplinaire teams en promoot je teams die samenwerken op verschillende niveaus.
De kunst van storytelling optimaliseren door middel van cijfers en effectieve visualisatietechnieken.
Analytisch en georganiseerd te werk en heb je zowel een oog voor detail als voor het grotere geheel.
Gefocust op continue verbetering en het automatiseren van huidige processen.
Nieuwsgierig te werk, stel je voldoende vragen om dieper in de stof te duiken en aarzel je niet om de status quo uit te dagen.
Proactief te werk met het zoeken naar verbetermogelijkheden met betrekking tot team, processen en data.

Je komt terecht in het Transaction Banking Data Domain, een team van ruim 40 data professionals in Nederland en India. De sfeer is open, informeel en ondernemend, met veel ruimte voor kennisdeling, persoonlijke ontwikkeling en initiatief. Diversiteit, inclusie en de waarden Care, Courage & Collaboration staan centraal in alles wat we doen.

Diploma in STEM of economie/bedrijfskunde, met een focus op analytics.
Minimaal 3 jaar werkervaring, waarvan minimaal 2 jaar op analytisch gebied.
Vaardigheid in programmeertalen zoals SQL of Python.
Ervaring met datavisualisatie tools zoals PowerBI of Tableau.
Kennis over datawarehouse-concepten en datamodelleringstechnieken.
Initiële kennis in Advance Analytics & AI technieken (Forecasting, Prediction, Cluster Analysis, Machine Learning & GenAI).
Een sterke combinatie van analytische vaardigheden, intellectuele nieuwsgierigheid, communicatieve en rapportagevaardigheden.
Uitstekende schriftelijke en mondelinge communicatieve vaardigheden in het Nederlands en het Engels.

Ervaring met werken op azure/ databricks/ of andere cloud platforms.
Kennis van de agile methodologie en het vermogen om verschillende prioriteiten gelijktijdig te managen.
Kennis van Data Warehouse technieken en data modellering technieken.
Kennis van de financiële sector en/of bankproducten.

Een uitstekende pensioenregeling, zodat je goed voorbereid bent voor later.
Flexibiliteit in werken: thuiswerken is mogelijk in overleg met je team en afhankelijk van je functie. Wij regelen een ergonomische thuiswerkplek voor je.
Ruimte voor ontspanning met vijf weken vakantie per jaar, aangevuld met twee verplichte vrije dagen. Daarnaast kun je jaarlijks tot vier extra weken vakantie bijkopen.

cao

persoonlijke bank in de digitale tijd

title: Senior Data Scientist - AI Strategy Team

You are an experienced professinoal that doesn't just build smart AI solutions, you shape the future of how we work.

We run several (Gen)AI applications, from data quality optimization models to automated reporting and signalling clients in distress, all used daily by colleagues across the organization.

title: Graduation internship | Harness Engineering for AI-Assisted Legacy Code Refactoring
description:
About this position
Across all domains of software engineering, the use of generative AI coding agents has proliferated, with 90% of professional software developers using them at work every week. Developers use them for tasks such as code comprehension, refactoring and generation.
Agent harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi are the infrastructure that transforms an LLM into a coding agent. Harnesses are responsible for tasks like preparing context, coordinating tools and tracking the agent’s state.
At TNO-ESI, we have developed tools for agents to integrate external data into their workflows. We have observed that, with the same underlying LLM, agents use these tools differently when paired with different harnesses, and even with different versions of the same harness.
This raises many open questions. How do harnesses select, compare and update context during a task? How much of our tools’ output reaches the model, and in what form? Can open-source harnesses compete with proprietary ones such as Claude Code and GitHub Copilot? To better understand the field of harness engineering, we are looking for a motivated and curious student to lay the foundations.
What will be your role?
TNO-ESI is working together with the high-tech equipment industry to research new methodologies for legacy code rejuvenation. The goal of this thesis project is to build knowledge of harness engineering, specifically how engineers can best use harnesses to address challenges in managing, refactoring and understanding legacy codebases. Tentative steps could include:
Conduct a literature review of state-of-the-art research on relevant aspects of harness engineering, identify gaps in the literature and select research questions.
Locally install and run a range of open-source harnesses such as Pi, OpenCode and Cline, read their source code and document their key architectural features and components, focusing on how they manage context, execution loops and system state.
Design and run a series of experiments on a legacy codebase, using the same LLM across a series of harnesses:
Build a small task set covering code analysis and refactoring, with evaluation criteria for each task.
Black-box comparison: evaluate the complete harnesses studied in Step 2, plus a state-of-the-art commercial harness (Claude Code or Codex) as a reference point, on the task set.
White-box comparison: using the knowledge from Step 2, vary the architecture and components (e.g. the context management strategy) within a configurable harness of your choice to isolate and understand their effect.
Study the execution traces to compare how each harness uses the available information, the quality of its output and what causes failure or unexpected behaviour.
Create design guidelines for future tools that interact with these harnesses, based on your findings.
Write and defend a thesis and optionally publish the results as an academic paper.
Optionally contribute to an open-source harness based on your findings.
What we expect from you
You are a Computer Science, Software Engineering or Computer Engineering MSc student looking for a graduation assignment. You are interested in how generative AI is applied in software development, and in the infrastructure that makes AI coding agents work.
You are comfortable working with large and unfamiliar codebases and have experience with TypeScript/JavaScript, as most of the agent harnesses you’ll study are built using these languages. Familiarity with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or alternatives is an advantage.
You are excited about developing new knowledge and contributing to an applied research project in collaboration with industry.

title: Internship | Energy-Based Models for Compositional Image Generation
description:
About this position
Modern image generators are remarkably good at generating familiar concepts, but still struggle with unusual combinations of otherwise familiar things. A model may easily generate a horse or a Formula 1 car individually, yet have more difficulty generating “a Formula 1 car next to a horse.” This challenge is particularly relevant in niche domains, where training data is limited and specific combinations may rarely occur.
Energy-based models (EBMs) offer a glimpse of what the next generation of generative models could look like: more compositional, controllable, and grounded in explicit constraints. In this project, you will explore whether EBMs can offer a different perspective on compositional image generation. One possible direction is to use energy functions to guide an existing diffusion or flow-based image generator, for example through separate guidance for objects, attributes, spatial relationships, or domain knowledge.
Another possible direction is to train smaller energy-based generative models directly, for example at 64 x 64 or 128 x 128 resolution in a constrained domain. This provides a controlled setting for investigating how well EBMs learn individual concepts and whether those concepts can be combined in ways that were rare or unseen during training. The exact direction is deliberately open, and we welcome students who want to develop or propose alternative ideas.
What will be your role?
You will study relevant work on energy-based and compositional generation, design and implement a suitable experimental approach, and evaluate it on a challenging domain where access to data is limited. Depending on your interests, the project may focus on guiding a pretrained generative model, training smaller EBMs directly, comparing both approaches, or another suggested alternative by you.
You will investigate when energy-based methods help, where they fail, and how different concepts or constraints interact during generation. This can give insight in how to improve our image generation approaches, specifically when rare combinations are concerned. The precise focus and methods can be tailored to match your interests and strengths.
During your internship, you will write a thesis documenting your research and we can provide you with computing power. If the results are promising, we may explore the possibility of a joint publication.
What we expect from you
You are in the final stages of your master’s degree in artificial intelligence, computer science, data science, or a related field. You have experience with Python and deep learning, and some familiarity with generative models. You are curious, comfortable with experimental research, and interested in helping shape the research question rather than only implementing a predetermined method.
We expect you to work from our office in The Hague (Oude Waalsdorperweg 63) at least two days per week, but preferably more often. Your supervision team will consist of experienced researchers in computer vision and deep learning who are actively involved in related projects. title: Projectmanager Collaborative Autonomous Systems
description:
About this position
Driven project managers are always welcome at TNO. Especially if you want to use your leadership skills to drive innovation in the defence and security domain. Apply for this vacancy and discover how you can contribute to a safer world.
The world of autonomous systems is evolving rapidly. These technological developments are transforming not only the systems themselves, but also the way civilian and military operations are designed and conducted. Within TNO’s Collaborative Autonomous Systems (CAS) department in The Hague, we develop innovative concepts, algorithms and software that enable teams of autonomous systems to work together reliably, optimally, robustly and effectively in complex operational environments.
With a multidisciplinary team of 35 scientists and engineers, CAS combines research with practical and operationally relevant solutions, taking innovations from concept to prototype and ultimately to fully operational systems. These systems are used, for example, for reconnaissance missions, surveillance operations and logistical support, where situational awareness, reliable navigation, including when GPS is limited or unavailable, and tactical effectiveness are essential. Through close collaboration with other TNO departments, the Ministry of Defence, industry partners and research institutes, our innovations quickly find their way into real-world applications.
To support this technological innovation, we are looking for a colleague to lead projects that enable the Ministry of Defence to operate more safely, quickly and effectively.
What will be your role?
As a project manager within the Collaborative Autonomous Systems (CAS) department, you are responsible for delivering project results on time and within budget. The nature of those results varies. One project may involve a feasibility study or analysis, while another may focus on developing a prototype.
You will always be working on several projects simultaneously, switching between different topics throughout your working day. You will often work on behalf of clients in the defence and security domain, such as the armed forces, and/or collaborate within large (EU) consortia and with industrial partners.
Close collaboration with these clients is a key part of your role, with a strong emphasis on customer intimacy. You develop a thorough understanding of the needs behind client requests, as well as the scope and interests involved in each project. Together with subject-matter experts, you then plan and organise the research while ensuring a high level of customer satisfaction.
Within your projects, you focus on delivering high-quality answers and solutions to clients while also strengthening your department’s knowledge base. Your projects will often involve:
Multidisciplinary, complex projects that span multiple departments.
Translating research into concept development and practical applications.
A strong focus on operational relevance.
Maintaining close alignment with clients and an outward-looking perspective.
Collaborating with a variety of partners and consortia, as well as with the Ministry of Defence and other research institutes.
Thanks to your leadership, project team members know what is expected of them and have the opportunity to develop their full potential. You pay particular attention to the development of early-career professionals within your team. You foster a positive and psychologically safe working environment, balancing individual needs with the interests of the team as a whole.
You also explore new ways to bring the knowledge developed within your department to the market. To achieve this, you work closely with subject-matter experts and business developers.
What we expect from you
You are a natural organiser who actively connects with internal and external stakeholders. You enjoy the challenge of getting complex projects on track and successfully bringing them to completion. You are equally comfortable communicating with technical professionals and with our clients, and you know how to translate the added value of our work into a message that resonates with stakeholders.
Together with your team, you know how to turn technical and scientific research into practical solutions for the international market. You are also a collaborative leader with excellent people-management skills. You have experience leading professionals through solution-oriented and servant leadership, and you know how to maintain calm and focus within the team during stressful situations.
You contribute to an inclusive culture in which we communicate openly, listen to one another and look out for each other. You encourage diversity and promote learning from each other’s experiments and ideas. You do all of this with one goal in mind: bringing our science and innovation to the front line.
What do you bring?
A relevant completed degree at a university of applied sciences (HBO) or research university (WO), with an affinity for the technical domain.
At least 3 to 5 years of experience as a project manager in a technical, research or development-focused environment.
Experience in, or a demonstrable affinity with, the defence and security domain.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written.
Strong leadership skills, with a collaborative, solution-oriented, facilitating and coaching approach.
Excellent command of both Dutch and English.
Why will you make a difference?
You will contribute to technology that enables the Ministry of Defence to operate more safely, quickly and effectively. Your collaborative leadership style and strong interpersonal and communication skills will help us build systems that make a real difference in operational environments.

Challenging and varied work with a real impact. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. We offer a gross monthly salary between € 4,800 and € 6,500 (based on your knowledge and experience), 8% holiday pay, a 13
th
